g.id: THREE OPTIONS for each system, plus OPTION 0 do nothing. Each is costed separately, on the same basis
Treated effluent sold: volume times price, capped by irrigation demand
Energy: pumping at the lifting stations, aeration at the plant
Gravity sewers priced by diameter AND depth band, manholes, house connections
STEP 3. Revenue and avoided cost, every year
Avoided cost: tanker haulage, septic emptying, deferring a new plant
Sewerage and connection charges, if NWS levies them
STEP 2. OPEX, built bottom-up, every year
Sludge, chemicals, labour, jetting, CCTV, odour control
Replacing mechanical and electrical plant inside the 25 years
STEP 1. CAPEX, phased across the construction years
Force mains, lifting stations, the STP at OMR per cubic metre per day, the TE network
Land, no-objection certificates, diversions, preliminaries and contingency
STEP 4. Discount every flow to today at 5 percent over 25 years: NET PRESENT VALUE and LIFE-CYCLE COST. Payback is reported but does not decide
STEP 6. Apply the weights NWS sets
STEP 7. Sensitivity: weighting, discount rate, design criteria
STEP 8. Tie-break: within 10 percent on lifetime cost the greener option wins
STEP 9. RECOMMENDED OPTION, one each for the sewer network, the TE network and the plant
